name: Mucinous adenocarcinoma of ovary

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and immunohistochemical diagnostic criteria for ovarian mucinous adenocarcinoma

criteria.description: Presence of malignant mucin-producing epithelial cells forming glandular structures in ovarian tissue
Positive staining for CK7 and variable CK20 expression supporting primary ovarian origin
Ovarian mass with cystic and solid components on pelvic ultrasound or MRI
Exclusion of metastatic mucinous carcinoma from gastrointestinal tract or other primary sites

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of mucinous adenocarcinoma in ovarian tissue with exclusion of metastatic disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Immunohistochemical profile and clinical correlation are essential to differentiate primary ovarian mucinous adenocarcinoma from metastatic mucinous tumors.

pathognomonic.notes: Often detected on physical examination or imaging

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abdominal distension due to tumor mass
pathognomonic.notes: Progressive enlargement of abdomen from tumor growth or ascites

common.notes: Usually dull or cramping in nature
Due to pressure on stomach from tumor
Accumulation of fluid in peritoneal cavity

occasional.notes: May be present in some patients
Secondary to mass effect or ascites
Due to chronic disease or blood loss
searchTerms: fatigue related to low red blood cells

rare.notes: Associated with advanced disease or metastasis

laboratory: Elevated CA-125 levels in some cases
Possible elevated tumor markers CEA and CA19-9
imaging: Ultrasound showing complex cystic and solid ovarian mass
MRI demonstrating multiloculated ovarian tumor with mucinous content
CT scan for staging and detection of metastases
genetic: KRAS mutations frequently observed in tumor tissue
Rare TP53 mutations in high-grade tumors
other: Histopathology revealing mucin-producing glandular epithelium with invasive growth
Immunohistochemistry positive for CK7, variable CK20, and negative for gastrointestinal markers in primary tumors

distinguishingFeatures: Immunohistochemistry positive for CK20 and CDX2
Histopathology showing serous rather than mucinous differentiation

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe abdominal pain indicating possible tumor rupture
Signs of bowel obstruction or ascites
references: Kurman RJ, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Female Reproductive Organs. 4th Edition. IARC; 2014.
Prat J. Ovarian carcinomas: five distinct diseases with different origins, genetic alterations, and clinicopathological features. Virchows Arch. 2012.
